req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with the same body for the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the PUT operation should be idempotent, meaning that repeated requests with the same data should not alter the state of the resource beyond the initial application. This is crucial for ensuring consistency in distributed systems where duplicate requests might occur. The test suite includes a positive test to confirm idempotency, a negative test to handle non-existent resources, and a boundary test to check behavior at the edge of valid input.

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_positive
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 1
Send identical PUT request to update task with id 1
expected: Task state remains unchanged after second request
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Initial PUT request
response1 = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Read chapter 5", "description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbor", "completed": true}
)
assert response1.status_code == 200

# Repeated PUT request
response2 = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Read chapter 5", "description": "Signal pulse ember orbit harbor", "completed": true}
)
assert response2.status_code == 200

# Verify idempotency
assert response1.json() == response2.json()

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_negative
preconditions: Task with id 999 does not exist
actions: Send PUT request to update non-existent task with id 999
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Attempt to update a non-existent task
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/999",
    json={"title": "Non-existent task", "description": "This task does not exist", "completed": false}
)
assert response.status_code == 404
assert response.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 999 not found"

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_boundary
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 20
Send identical PUT request to update task with id 20
expected: Task state remains unchanged after second request
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

# Initial PUT request
response1 = client.put(
    "/tasks/20",
    json={"title": "Reply to emails", "description": "Summit cascade willow zenith pulse beacon ember willow.", "completed": false}
)
assert response1.status_code == 200

# Repeated PUT request
response2 = client.put(
    "/tasks/20",
    json={"title": "Reply to emails", "description": "Summit cascade willow zenith pulse beacon ember willow.", "completed": false}
)
assert response2.status_code == 200

# Verify idempotency
assert response1.json() == response2.json()
